articleTitle: LOGISTIQUA 2018 Plenary Talks
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the plenary presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Outsourcing of Logistics’ Activities: Impact Analysis on Logistics Service Performance
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Logistic is one of the functions that companies are currently outsourcing. The decision to keep this function in-house or to contract with one or many logistic service providers (LSP) is entirely strategic and can have a significant impact on the bottom line. As a result, the outsourcing of logistics activities plays a vital role in making thoses activities more efficient and effective and have a greater impact on the performance of the logistic services. Numerous aspects of the topic of LSP issue have been covered in the foregoing studies (Hofer et al., 2009), however, very little are known analyzing the impact of the use of these providers on the performance of companies. The objective of this artice is to analyze the impact of the outsourcing of logistics activities according to four levels. The article concludes by presenting the likely recommendations and conclusions on how companies can move forward with the outsourced logistic activities.

articleTitle: Road accident modeling approaches: literature review
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The apprehension of the problem of road accidents was the subject of several investigations. To this end, different approaches were developed. The aim of our work is to provide a synthesis of various approaches developed in the field of road safety, their principles, and the characteristics of the developed models according to these approaches. We started with a presentation of each approach, and models that apprehend the problem of road accidents. Finally, a synthesis table is presented to facilitate reading and characterizing each type of approach.

articleTitle: How can Top management succeed in a lean manufacturing implementation in the small and medium sized enterprises?
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This work aims to study the key principles of Lean Manufacturing and our goal through this study is to achieve change within companies. The literature has shown that leadership and management are among the critical aspects critical to successful Lean deployment. Knowledge of the principles of leadership and management is a fundamental step to ensure the commitment of management, the participation of all employees and to lead to change.

articleTitle: Port Logistics Optimization Model Study
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The current situation characterized by the fierce competition between the various ports and the need to maximize their yields, pushes all the port stakeholders and mainly the port authorities, shipping companies and terminal operators..., to think about the design and the development of a policy of scheduling and priority management of vessels movements at the port. This project aim to give a prediction regarding the congestion period in order to reduce the waiting time (operational loss) of vessels during their stay at the port, increase traffic and port competitiveness, and lead to higher revenues, by keeping optimal level of customer satisfaction. This project took place at the planning service of vessel call in the port Tanger Med into the company “Tanger Med Port Authority” and the present report summarizes the conducted work and the methodology behind. The aim of this research consists of developing a system able to give forecasts on the periods of congestion of vessel harbour moves, in order to make a strategic decision and to optimize vessels calls productivity. The objective is to elaborate a system, which contains all the aspects of the activity and the operational process, by choosing the most relevant KPI that perfectly represent port vessels moves congestion. First, we had to conduct an analysis to identify the causes of delay that affect the most the global performance. Moreover, we had to identify all the aspects and indicators that should describe the situation of congestion and port operations. Then, the development of the system to give forecasts on the periods of congestion. In addition, this research depends on a number of criteria and variables such as: Port configuration, vessel type and characteristic, quay availability, meteorological conditions as well as the availability of the access channel and harbour basin, as well as the concept of safety, which remains an essential element throughout the process of making vessels calls.

articleTitle: Towards an ontological approach to company compenteces management
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new approach concerning the ontological model of competence based on the Deming wheel in order to facilitate the communication and understanding of information that ensures proper competence management of resources within the company. Ontology constitutes a pertinent mean to define and to manage competencies and knowledge in companies thanks to its suitability to model knowledge. In this work, we develop a model that describes the management of competencies in order to improve processing and sharing of information.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis the simultaneous scheduling problems of production and maintenance activities
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Extensively of the scheduling theory assumes that machines are always available to process jobs at any time during the scheduling horizon. However, machines may be unavailable for various reasons in realistic practices. This article studies a comparative analysis of simultaneous scheduling problems of production and maintenance activities in the flow shop. Our literature review focuses first on the basic concepts of scheduling problems. Subsequently, we focus our attention on the principal methods for solving scheduling problems, while presenting in the following the main published works for the aforementioned systems. Lastly, a comparative analysis is carried out to highlight the fundamental ideas leading to the adoption of an effective approach capable of producing an optimal solution in a reasonable calculation time.

articleTitle: Territorial Logistics Governance and Sustainable Development Challenges : (Analysis and evaluation of the logistics competitiveness of the Casablanca-Settat region)
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is twofold. First, it is about situating our study of the governance of territorial logistics by answering certain questions. How logistics can participate in the development of the territories? How to reconcile the obligation of companies' competitiveness with the imperative of the sustainable territorial development? In other words, how to give a determining place of the territorial logistics within the framework of the sustainable development approach? The second purpose is to measure and analyze the logistics competitiveness of the Casablanca-Settat region. The result of this study is considered the paper's major contributions and its provide a review of the logistics competitiveness of the region. However, further studies are needed for the other regions of Morocco in order to have a clear vision of regional logistics performance and to support territorial logistics governance in the context of the advanced regionalisation adopted in Morocco.

articleTitle: Optimizing subcontracting choice in the context of integrated maintenance into production
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This article addresses the problem of integrated maintenance and production management for a manufacturing system. The latter is subject to a random failure and characterized by a maximum production rate. With a view to meet a constant demand over time and greater than the maximum production capacity, the company uses outsourcing. Therefore, there are two strategies for selecting subcontractors. The first strategy is to make an optimal choice of a single subcontractor. The second strategy is characterized by switching between two subcontractors. Moreover, the choice between the subcontractors is based on several data. Consequently, the objective is to verify the results and evaluate the performance of the reference model [1]. This model optimizes simultaneously the different costs: maintenance, production and lost orders by simultaneously determining the optimal age of preventive maintenance and the switching date between subcontractors.

articleTitle: Efficient Approach for Parallel Machine Scheduling Problem
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a parallel machine scheduling problem with non-renewable resources. Each job consumes several components and must be processed in one stage composed of identical parallel machines. Resources availability operations, jobs assignment and sequencing are considered and optimized simultaneously. In order to find an optimal solution, an exact method is applied to optimize the total completion time. Due to the problem complexity and prohibitive computational time to obtain an exact solution, a metaheuristic approach based genetic algorithm is proposed and several heuristics are adapted to solve it. Moreover, the impact of non-renewable resources procurement methods on production scheduling is analyzed. The system performances are evaluated in terms of measures such as the solution quality and the execution time. The simulation results show that the proposed genetic algorithm gives the same results as the exact method for small instances and performs the best compared to heuristics for medium and large instances.

articleTitle: Innovation: The Linking & the impact of the variables “Knowledge management” and “Organizational culture” on the company’s performance
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: We call “Knowledge Management” all the tools, methods and approaches implemented in society to identify, capitalize the knowledge of the company, to organize and to share it. The purpose of our paper is to discuss the important role that Knowledge management plays in the process of sustainability of companies; likewise our aim will be to discover the relation between the organizational culture, innovation and knowledge management.

articleTitle: Quality Control In Laboratories of Medical Biology (LBM): the Statistical Process Control (SPC)
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The quality has become more important in our society and in the health field as well. It is more deployed specifically in medical laboratories (LAMB). Since September 2010, the medical biology in Morocco is governed by the Guide of Good Execution of Analyzes (GGEA) * [1, 2]. However, in the third chapter, Quality Assurance, the GGEA recommends internal quality control. This control is a fundamental issue in the implementation of the quality assurance approach in LMBs [3]. Beyond its enforceable character, it remains an important condition for the success and for the effectiveness of external quality control [4]. 13% of NC * [4] are detected in the analytical phase in despite of the automation of its analysis process and the permanent acquisition of the last generation of the automats. LMBs work practically with Shewhart standards which is fixing a specific level and area of trust for statistical process control [5]. Each sector has its realities and its statistical standards and they must be, the both, fixed and adapted to each sector, activity or parameter. They must be studied again in despite of all the random and assignable causes of process variability. In this context that we perform this study on statistical process control in LMBs to show the temporal evolution of a process and to detect the possible changes to modify its performance. This study shows the interest of the application of these methods coming from the industrial environment for monitoring and improving the quality of a process in the field of transfusion. It also highlights the difficulties caused by the retrospective search for the sources of uncontrolled variations of a process. To do this, we carry out a statistical study with the standards, to re-fixit and make a comparative study of the two to appreciate the effectiveness of each control and the performance of the biochemical analyzer Konelab 20i at the laboratory of medical biology analysis CASABARATA.

Author Keywords: Laboratory of Analysis of Medical Biology (LAMB)
Guide of Good Execution of Analyzes (GGEA)

articleTitle: Importance of Information technologies and systems (ITS) in the traceability of the supply chain
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: In front of numerous challenges been imperative by the globalization of the trade, the uncertainty of the environment, the new requirements of the consumers, He is essential for any company to be equipped with tools, ways and effective technologies allowing them to identify the information, to record them, to exchange them and to share them with the partners. Because today the paper traceability is not any more a reliable option according to [1]. The traceability mobilizes an outfit of systems and technological devices. Indeed, the objective of this paper is double: at first, raise a current situation of the various technologies and the information systems used in an approach of traceability. Then, identify them role in the traceability of the supply chain.

articleTitle: The reconfigurability of a hospital center facing a massive influx of victims
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The aim of this work is to introduce an efficient way for the management and the sizing of a hospital center facing exceptional situations as a result of a massive influx of victims. The purpose of this study is to provide hospitals with a powerful immune system that can respond quickly to unexpected situations. This system suggests a process of organization and management of such situations from the reception of the information to the filtering of victims. Then, we will have to find our needs in human and material resources for the process input. This process is modelled using ARENA software. A case study was carried out in the prefectural hospital center (PHC) ALMANSOR in Casablanca (Morocco) to determine the different situations, especially in the emergency department (ED). The purpose is to work on the cases of recorded mass influxes.

articleTitle: A new efficient metaheuristic for solving the Uncapacitated Single Allocation p-Hub Median Problem
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Hub location problem is an NP-hard problem, it deals with finding the location of hub facilities and allocating the demand nodes to these hub facilities so as to effectively route the demand between any origin-destination pair. In this paper, we study the Uncapacitated Single Allocation p-Hub Median Problem (USApHMP) variant of the hub location problems. Thus, we present a new and robust solution based on artificial immune system (AIS) framework for this problem. The outcome of this paper is a new approach in the form of clonal selection algorithm (CSA) to solve this location-allocation problem. The algorithm maintains the feasibility of individuals by using a specific representation. To the best of our knowledge, this methodology of solving the USApHMP is introduced to the literature for the first time.

articleTitle: DSS design for carrier collaboration using Big graph & IOT
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This paper describes a DSS Decision support system architecture based on Big Data and IOT technologies, for supporting and improving decision-making in the context of carrier collaboration. Indeed advances in Big Data technologies have improved the creation of intelligent and powerful environments for a number of complex issues, such as the case discussed in this paper concerning the collaboration of transport providers. We will provide a conceptual model of DSS as multilayers architecture, which offers a set of services, namely the transport optimization that favor the efficiency of vehicle fleet operations, the collection and integration of real-time data sent by in-vehicle IOT technologies, allowing analysis and Realtime tracking of vehicles as well as freight. Through dashboards, decision makers can visualize the details of operations and interact according to system recommendations.

articleTitle: Literature review on successful JIT implementation in developing countries : obstacles and critical success factors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The importance of new and modern systems in the industrial world has increased in the last decade because of the advantages that they bring to the industries. Just-in-time is considered as one of these new systems that receive more attention in developed countries, however developing countries are still unaware of the importance of this system because of the obstacles that prevent it from being successful. In this article, we will discuss some of the obstacles faced by firms when introducing JIT into their operations, drawing from published research about manufacturing organisations in developing countries. The study enables to conclude that there are many difficulties that face just-in-time implementation, but the lack of management commitment is considered the most important obstacle that prevent just-in-time understanding and success. The employees and suppliers are also some of the major obstacles that face JIT implementation. To overcome these obstacles, critical success factors of JIT implementation must be understood, starting from improving production strategy, management commitment, choosing the right and better workers, finding the right suppliers, and finally trying to decrease all inventory types to the lowest possible level.

articleTitle: Towards a tool for modeling the vulnerability of processes in project management in an industrial context
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The project management system plays a fundamental role in ensuring the continuity of the project phases with milestones defined by the project team. Indeed, the main concern of project managers is to ensure their smooth running with a minimum of risk. This article introduces a new thinking on project risk management. For this reason, the concept of vulnerability of a process in the project management system is introduced as well as the relation between the elementary vulnerability of a process and the global vulnerability. The objective, then, is to provide managers of industrial projects with a quantitative vulnerability assessment model by introducing the vulnerability index and its factors. This tool will highlight and quantify the inherent weaknesses in project management processes in order to identify and control potential risks that may arise from them.

articleTitle: A performance comparison between hybrid and neighbourhood genetic algorithm applied to assembly line balancing problem
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The lively field of assembly line balancing often have a significant impact on the performance of production systems. In this context, assembly line balancing problem (ALBP) are widely cited in the literature, and known to be NP-hard in general. For the resolution of such problem, a genetic algorithm (GA) is implemented to solve ALBP. There are two objectives to be achieved: to maximize the line efficiency, and to balance the workload between workstations. The GA may lack the capability of exploring the solution space effectively. To improve the search performance of GA, we have adapted two methods to the classical GA, one is a hybridization of GA which is performed by a priority rule-based procedure aiming at seeding the initial population with good solutions, and other one is GA adopted with strategy of localized evolution. Through computational experiments using ten test problems collected from literature, the performance comparison between GAs is performed and the results are reported.

articleTitle: Lean Manufacturing: Study Concept for Collective Intelligence Definition and validation of the conceptual model : Definition and validation of the conceptual model
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Our study aims to study the relationship between the sustainability of Lean and the use of collective intelligence (CI) as a participative management tool, and to define collective intelligence at Lean, in light of the definitions of others disciplines. Then demonstrate that Lean represents a fertile concept for the study of collective intelligence in its most basic form which is the intelligence of teams limited in number and space. This study will be used to develop the concept for broader areas, and to follow up a tool for measuring and managing collective intelligence in Lean.

articleTitle: Analytical Study of Transfer of Manufacturing Capacities Basing on Financial Criteria
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Multinational firms are undeniably confronted with great competition and must make strategic choices to increase their profit and ensure their sustainability. The geographical choice of subsidiaries or the relocation of existing ones to other countries are among the crucial decisions of the supply chain management and have a significant impact on the company's portfolio. These types of decisions are often motivated by logistical advantages, as well as by the tax discount offered by host countries. Through this article we present an analytical model of decision making tool for the geographical choice of subsidiaries taking into account the financial constraints of potential destinations. Through a case study, we evaluate the impact of financial policies and specially the transfer pricing policies on the choice of subsidiaries and the amount of manufacturing capacity to relocate. The established model will be a powerful tool for decision-making concerning the delocalization of subsidiaries.

articleTitle: On the assessment of the individual competence level for an environmental manager: Case of logistics sector
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The aim of the present work is to provide a decision making tool that allows recruiting an environmental manager able to lead an environmental management system in a logistics platform. For that purpose, an approach based on the fuzzy representation model 2-tuple and TOPSIS (Technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution) method is used. According to the ISO 14001:2015 standard, a competency framework for the environmental manager has been developed. This framework represents an input for the evaluation process. In order to implement the approach, a software has been developed under JAVA, named ECM (Environmental Competence Management) easy to use for assessing the candidates according to the identified competencies. ECM provides as an output, the ranking of the candidates according to the competencies evaluated by the experts.

articleTitle: A disjunctive graph for the Job Shop Problem with Transport and blocking no wait constraints
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This paper addresses the scheduling problem of job shop with transport and Blocking no wait constraints. This NP-Hard problem is an extension of the classical job shop problem that take into account transport operations by several robots and the absence of storage space between machines.. The objective is to determine a schedule of machine and transport operations as well as an assignment of robots to transport operations with minimal makespan. The problem can be efficiently modeled by a disjunctive graph and any solution can be fully defined by an orientation of the graph. We formulate the problem by means of a new disjunctive graph. We present a solution representation based on two vectors. We modelized blocking situations and described properties of partial schedule that lead to deadlock situations. The new disjunctive graph and deadlock situations properties served us to develop a greedy heuristics based on priority and avoiding blocking cycle rules. Computational results are reported. This paper is a step forward definition of an efficient approach for the resolution of the job shop problem with several robots and blocking no wait constraints.

articleTitle: Does trust influence the success of SCM? Case of actors in the fruits and vegetables sector in the region Souss Massa-Morocco
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: in the same way of our research about Supply chain management, we have noticed in the Moroccan context, and especially in the agricultural sector, informal holds an important place in relations. So we wanted to study the role that trust could play in the establishment, sustainability and success of relations between SC partners. This led us to carry out an exploratory study, in order to have answers to the various questions concerning this subject. And above all to demonstrate if the theorical finding in literature can be applied to the Moroccan context. We will begin our paper by explaining the key concepts on which our research will be based, trust, supply chain management and related concepts. We will then present our working methodology and the results of the qualitative study, which we conducted with a group of players in the fruit and vegetable sector in the region of Souss Massa.

articleTitle: The interaction between industry 4.0 and smart logistics: concepts and perspectives
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This work generally deals with the state of art of the three industrial revolutions that formed the basis of the current fourth industrial revolution. Thus, it deals in particular with the context and the characteristics of the fourth industrial revolution. This revolution consists of four elements that are Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), Internet of Things IOT, Internet Services (IOS) and Smart Factory. The appearance of Industry 4.0 prompted researchers to develop a new logistic concept called “smart logistics” to accompany the progress of Industry 4.0, which motivated us to look for the stages of development of logistics, through the four industrial revolutions up to “smart logistics” and define this new concept of logistics to facilitate its implementation in practice. This article also discusses the prospects for future researches in the field of smart.

articleTitle: The Determinants of the performance of the Urban Freight Transport - An Empirical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: In this article, we are interested in identifying the factors determining the performance of the Urban Freight Transport (UFT) and measuring the impact of each factor. To do this, we conducted a literature review of theoretical and empirical work that addressed this topic. At the end of this literature review, we formulated a set of hypotheses explaining the influence relationships between the factors identified and the performance of the UFT. To test the veracity of these hypotheses, we conducted an empirical study based on the Structural Equation Modeling estimated by the Partial Least Square (PLS) method. Our empirical analysis is based on data from a survey of the freight transport managers and users in the city of Fes. The scientific interest of this work is to present the decision makers of the city of Fez with recommendations to improve the development of freight transport.

articleTitle: A Model Integrating a Smart Approach to Support the National Port Strategy for a Horizon of 2030
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The economy of a nation cannot be dissociated from shipping, port infrastructure and storage of goods. Indeed, the mastery of the port logistic chain is a crucial issue. In this context, the Kingdom of Morocco has set up a national port strategy by 2030 “SPN2030” to support the port reform of December 2005; this strategy aims to develop the ports in order to improve the competitiveness of the national economy. Major investments in excess of MDH 60 billion, and considerable resources are expected by this strategy in order to help Morocco join the developed countries. It is then necessary that the ports contribute to its success by using smart strategies. Among these smart port strategies: Smart-ports that are currently present in various continents with different models, integrating the functional aspects and the organizational dimension. However smart-ports are not enough, an effective smart approach should be implemented to better support the ”SPN2030” and ensure its effectiveness. First of all, it would be necessary to relate the ”SPN2030” with its strengths and potentially its weak points, before to define the smart port. Then we’ll propose a smart approach to better support the ”SPN2030” and guarantee its effectiveness relative to internal and external hazards. In this article, we present a model with the UML language of the ”SPN2030” integrating a smart approach in the sectorial strategies concerned by the ”SPN2030” and making it possible to contribute to the performance of the ports.

articleTitle: Elaboration of an association matrix of satisfaction factors in healthcare facilities and hospital logistics activities
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: the main objective of this paper is to highlight the link between the quality of care and hospital logistics activities.Patient satisfaction is one of the major objectives of the quality of care, but also the satisfaction of healthcare professionals is required to ensure a good quality care. To improve patient satisfaction on the one hand, and the satisfaction of healthcare professionals on the other hand, hospital logistics could play a crucial role. Indeed, after identifying the elements that contribute to satisfaction, it turned out that numerous factors affecting patient satisfaction (waiting time, hotel services, etc.) and job satisfaction of healthcare professionals (work environment, availability of resources, proper planning, etc.),fall within hospital logistics scope. This relationship between satisfaction and hospital logisticsis clarified by the elaboration of an association matrix that establishes the dependency link between satisfaction factors in healthcare facilities and hospital logistics activities. Consequently, the improvement of the efficiency of such logistics is a great tool to increase the level of satisfaction for both patients and healthcare professionals.This paper was developed based on a concise analysis and synthesis of research studies that dealt with the following topics: patient satisfaction, job satisfaction, healthcare professionals and hospital logistics.

articleTitle: An analysis of public bus transport performance and its determinants factors: The case of major Morocco's cities
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to evaluate and compare the performance of six public bus companies operating in the main Moroccan cities for the year of 2013 and to identify, at the same time, the external factors that affect the estimated performance. To this end, the “two-stage Data Envelopment Analysis (D.A.E) approach” was adopted. As a first step, the production efficiency, operational effectiveness and overall performance of operators were measured using three separate DEA models. In the second step, some external “environmental” factors are regressed on performance scores using a Tobit regression model.

articleTitle: A SCOR based Performance evaluation system of the Hospital Supply chain
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The literature on Hospital Supply Chain performance is limited and assessing the performance of the Hospital Supply Chain (HSC) is currently a key challenge. The sector has to balance the seemingly incompatible demand of cost reduction and quality improvement. Despite hospital supply chain having a great impact on hospital budgets, opportunities for optimization still exist and can be identified through performance measurement in order to enhance healthcare quality and have a harmonious relationship between care providers and patients. The developed SCOR metrics measurement system is a balanced set of financial and non-financial measures. The purpose of this study is to discuss the applicability of the SCOR performance system and evaluate the HSC performance based on five aspects i.e. Reliability, Responsiveness, Agility, Costs and Asset Management Efficiency. The main contribution of this paper is to improve practical performance and enhances management effectiveness for HSC. This study applies the Multiple Criteria Decision Making methods (MCDM) to evaluate the HSC performance. In general the service quality has abstract properties, which mean that using the previously known measurement approach is insufficient. A generalized quantitative evaluation model based on the Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchical Process (FAHP) was then used to consider both the interdependence among measures and the fuzziness of subjective measures in HSC.

articleTitle: Improving performance through measurement: the application of BSC and AHP in healthcare organization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This paper introduces a conceptual framework for evaluating performance in healthcare organizations. The challenge of evaluating performance resides in the determination of the appropriate model with the appropriate indicators that meet the characteristics of the framework. In this end, our study is based on the development of structured approach for evaluating performance for hospitals in Morocco. The scope of this study is developed through three main phases. First, related literature of performance measurement systems was conducted, to identify the appropriate model to our context. Second, after analyzing different PMS, we have found that BSC presents the convenient one to hospitals. Based on the literature review and panel of experts, we determined the criteria, sub-criteria and key performance indicators (KPIs). Third, the relative weights of the chosen evaluators were calculated by Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) technique. The analysis results highlight the critical aspects of evaluation criteria as well as the gaps to enhance hospital performance for achieving desired target. This model can be a useful tool for evaluating and comparing the performance of hospitals.

articleTitle: Lean Service Practices in the Moroccan Banking Sector (Agadir agencies)
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: For more than twenty years, the Lean Management approach knew a huge success in improving the performance of industrial companies. After benefiting from the gains of this approach in their production lines, Lean Management allowed the diffusion of Japanese methods in all types of companies (from the multinational to the very small company) and in all activity sectors. Today, Lean Management is proving more and more its legitimacy in services, especially in the banking sector. Indeed, the Moroccan banking structures constitute an interesting field of action for the implementation of the Lean service approach. A better application of the Lean service proves an improvement in its maturity level. Thus, to investigate the relationship between Lean service practices and the maturity level, banking firms were surveyed about the application of Lean service practices. Subsequently, based on a comparative approach, and from a qualitative survey, we seek to determine the Lean service practices used to achieve a higher level of maturity. This qualitative approach, based mainly on a scoring questionnaire, enabled us to determine the maturity criteria of the Lean service approach in the Moroccan banking sector, calculate the maturity level of the Lean service and finally classify the banks according to their maturity score.

articleTitle: Improvement of the Municipal Waste Collection : The real case of city center of Tlemcen, Algeria
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: In a time where environmental impact is important, even the little contribution is welcome, like the Chinese philosopher Lao-Tzu says “a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step”. We present here an application of the multiple traveling salesman problem (m-TSP) for the improvement of the operation of waste collection. We used a simulated annealing heuristic for the purpose and compare the results with the optimization by the lingo solver. Both of them give excellent results for small instances but only the simulated annealing go so far and give an acceptable solution for all the instances. Real data were taken from the field by using an android application “GeoTracker” and real distances are calculated by using the open source software “Google maps”, an n by n asymmetric matrix D is then generated and data was treated by using the two methods.

articleTitle: Identification of quality manager’s competencies by the AHP method
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Competencies management has become a key to companies' success and perennity. The present work consists of developing a model for identification of critical requisite competencies applied for the first time for a quality management system QMS, within the framework of an evaluation process of competencies. In this article, we explain our approach by the Post of a quality manager. Consequently, we have developed a new reference table of Required competencies dedicated to the QMS system which response the new exigencies of the standard ISO 9001 with its new version 2015, by proposing a referential demarche and a prioritization approach of requested competencies and we are implementing the AHP method (Hierarchical Process Analysis) in order to identify and prioritize competencies relating to the quality manager, which constitutes an input data for the evaluation of candidates by experts.

articleTitle: Model of a maintenance process improvement approach inclusioning Lean Six Sigma and Preventive Maintenance optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Changes in the business environment have led companies to look for new ways to improve their performance. In fact, faced with a rapid internationalization of trade and exacerbated competition, manufacturers around the world have adopted rationalization and optimization policies. This research work aims to propose the most advanced approach to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of maintenance.

articleTitle: Multi-agent architecture for managing return flows
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The reverse logistics process is trigged by the companies back flow. This type of logistics, leading to green logistics chain, is attracting the researchers and industries attention. This article aims to suggest a multiple -agent system computing that can manage the return flows. Our approach starts with an establishment of existing works assessments among scientific publications, then we proceed with a presentation of our own system features and characteristic functions.

articleTitle: Shared values, a determinant key of the organizational culture in the context of HSC Case of Cheikh Khalifa Hospital
publicationTitle: 2018 International Colloquium on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This article aims to highlight the causal relationship between values sharing and organizational culture in the Hospital Supply Chain (HSC) context, case of the Moroccan hospital Cheikh Khalifa (HCK). It attempts to identify the dimensions of sharing the most significant values and those that influence the exchange relationship between HSC internal actors. Conducting semi-structured interviews with all HSC Cheikh Khalifa actors (administrators, doctors, pharmacists and nurses) helps to achieve our goal.
